feat(outreach): consent bridge, lawful channel router and evidence beacon

When cold email is not lawful for a prospect (the recipient's country
requires consent, the sender's own country regulates electronic marketing,
or no transport permits cold B2B) the prospect used to be a dead end. These
three organs, generated through GENESIS and bound to founder moonshots,
route it through a first touch the prospect can answer:

  channels (letter, partner introduction, in person, founder network).
  Codes carry no personal data, expire, revoke and redeem idempotently;
  redemption creates the prospect's own consent receipts. The public intake
  form now records ?code= as the lead source, and attributeBridgeLeads()
  maps those leads to channel and campaign with validity at request time.
- Lawful Channel Router (#790 Monoculture Detector, #107 Matter Router,
  #1 Causal Compiler; GENESIS "cross-domain translation"): per prospect,
  every route with its legal state and cost; cold email only when the
  eligibility engine PASSED; letters only to businesses, with founder
  authorization, budget and a provenance-backed address, and for EG/SA/AE
  senders only after a recorded counsel confirmation; suppression wins.
  Cohorts report spend, channel concentration and exactly what would
  unlock held routes.
- Evidence Beacon (#306 Proof-of-Value, #67 Trust Compiler, #146 Knowledge
  Packet; GENESIS "adversarial search"): the pitch is the prospect's own
  verifiable findings from the existing auditor, same-domain, recent,
  excerpted and confident, with no revenue claims; nothing qualifying means

feat(consent): evidence-grade consent receipts for the public intake (#161)

The public intake stored consent as a bare boolean, which cannot show what
was agreed, when, through which surface or for which purpose. CASL puts the
burden of proving consent on the sender and UK/EU GDPR requires consent to
be demonstrable, so a boolean is not usable evidence.

src/consent-receipt.mjs (founder moonshot #161, The Consent Protocol):
- receipts bind the exact versioned wording (hash), purposes, channel,
  source reference and capture time; the address and IP are stored only
  as digests;
- marketing consent starts PENDING_CONFIRMATION and becomes ACTIVE only
  with the HMAC confirmation token issued at capture, within 7 days;
- withdrawal outranks every earlier grant; a later re-grant counts again;
- consentRelationshipFor() returns the relationship and evidence reference
  the recipient-eligibility engine accepts, refusing on purpose, subject,
  pending, revoked, stale or tampered receipts.

A confirmed opt-in makes a recipient eligible where cold email is rejected
(tested with a German recipient and an Egypt-based sender). The public
intake now stores a sealed receipt for the exact sentence the form shows;
the legacy boolean is unchanged.

author: Claude
message:
fix(uberdns): never overwrite or duplicate live DNS the plan does not own

The GoDaddy adapter matched existing records by name and type only. For
TXT that meant publishing SPF on a root holding one unrelated TXT (a site
verification token, for example) replaced that token, and a root holding
two TXT records got an additional SPF even if one was already SPF, leaving
two SPF records, a permanent SPF error. An existing MX could also be
silently repointed.

TXT records are now reconciled by purpose (SPF / DMARC / DKIM / other):
only a same-purpose record is ever replaced, unrelated TXT is left alone,
and multiple same-purpose records refuse instead of adding another. The
GoDaddy default _dmarc record is replaced rather than duplicated. Changing
an existing MX requires an explicit allowMxReplacement flag. All zones
are read and every action decided before the first write, so a refusal
in one zone cannot leave another half-changed.

author: Claude
message:
feat(outreach): compile per-recipient legal eligibility from facts

The final launch gate hard-stops any recipient whose legal.status is not
PASSED, but nothing produced that status: the jurisdiction matrix was data
and compileOutboundLegalEvidence only records a decision made elsewhere.
Every real recipient therefore hard-stopped, whatever transport existed.

src/uberoutbound-recipient-eligibility.mjs decides one recipient from
supplied facts and returns ALLOW / ALLOW_WITH_REQUIREMENTS / HOLD_FOR_REVIEW
/ REJECT with the rule, the regulator source and the message obligations:

- US: CAN-SPAM opt-out regime for business recipients; aggravated
  harvesting refused; postal identity, truthful headers, non-deceptive
  subject, ad identification and a working opt-out are checked.
- GB: PECR corporate subscribers only; sole traders need consent; named
  employees additionally need an LIA reference and a privacy notice.
- CA / AU: conspicuous-publication implied consent only with a verified
  absence of a no-solicitation statement and role relevance; AU refuses
  automated harvesting.
- DE, CH, SA reject cold email; FR/other EU, AE, EG and every unencoded
  jurisdiction hold for review. Sender jurisdiction is required, and
  EG/SA/AE senders hold (Egypt PDPL electronic-marketing consent/licence).
- Suppression, guessed addresses, system mailboxes, stale or missing
  provenance and a transport whose terms forbid cold B2B dominate.

legal.status is PASSED only when every attached obligation is evidenced;
the object feeds evaluateOutreachLaunchGate unchanged. UberProspect now
requires that evidence-bearing decision instead of a bare legalEligible
boolean and carries the eligibility evidence id into each prospect.
No send, campaign, spend or authority is created.

Adds scripts/recipient-eligibility.mjs (npm run outreach:eligibility).
